newsitem.title: UK: British Christmas tree thieves striking early.
newsitem.headline: British Christmas tree thieves striking early.

text.p: British Christmas tree growers are employing night-time guards and installing trip wires and high fences in a bid to thwart thieves hoping to cash in on expected high prices.
Growers said on Saturday thieves were striking earlier than usual this year because a possible shortage of the trees was likely to push up prices.
"The thieves drive in with their lorries and just fill them up," said Mark Simms, who runs a 150-acre (60 hectares) plantation near London.
Tony Richardson, secretary of the British Christmas Tree Growers Association, has issued a warning to his 316 members about the increased threat from thieves.
"Everyone is using night-time patrols, trip wires, locked gates, ultra-violet beams which set off alarms. One retired general used to have a radar," said Richardson.
